title: Genesis Constraint-First Alignment Epistemology: Reason, Error, and World-Tracking under Irreducible Mediation

equations.meaning: Observation is always filtered by an agent-relative projection function Π_A representing sensory limitation, instrumental bandwidth, sampling constraints, and selective exposure.
Raw observation is encoded via T_A into a format metabolizable by the agent's conceptual, linguistic, or computational architecture (categorization, measurement conventions, theory-laden framing).
Model revision (update U_A): the next representation depends on the prior model, newly encoded observation, background constraints C_A, and an anomaly-sensitive resistance term Δ_A[n].
The central axiom of fallibilism: total epistemic error remains strictly greater than zero; perfect isomorphism between model and world is structurally unavailable to finite knowers.
Epistemic alignment is defined as domain-indexed (D): a model can be highly aligned for one set of tasks and poorly aligned for another, blocking overstatement of local success as global adequacy.

The framework's main normative claim: under repeatable conditions, disciplined reasoning (Rsn_A) tends to produce better expected epistemic alignment than leaving models unrevised under the same domain conditions.
